title: Zero-error time complexity class
statement: For a function $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{ZTIME}(T)$ be the class of languages over the Boolean alphabet that are decided by some nondeterministic Turing machine within time $cT(n)$ on inputs of length $n$, for some natural-number constant $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
There exist a natural-number constant $c$ and a nondeterministic Turing machine deciding the language within time $cT(n)$
